target.title: fix(android): improve chat UI spacing and compact tool bubbles
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the mobile chat UI readability and space issues in the Android app. The current chat interface has cramped bubbles, role labels on every message, and tool calls that take up excessive screen space.

## Changes

### `ChatScreen.kt`
- **Bubble width**: `0.56f`/`0.64f` → `widthIn(max=520dp)` — proper mobile proportions
- **Bubble padding**: `7dp/3.5dp` → `16dp/14dp` — breathing room inside bubbles
- **Bubble shape**: Directional — flat edge faces sender (ChatGPT-style)
- **Role labels removed**: No more "You"/"OpenClaw" on every message — position + color tell the story
- **Timestamps removed from inside bubbles**: Were visual noise on every turn
- **Font size**: Body `14sp` → `15sp`, line height `19sp` → `22sp`
- **Tool bubbles**: Collapsed into single compact card — "Ran N tools" header + monospace tool names, expandable for >2 tools
- **Thinking indicator**: Animated pulsing dots instead of text wall
- **Error suppression**: Chat errors no longer interrupt the chat list — surface in header status pill
- **Header**: Cleaner status labels ("Ready"/"Working…"/"Offline"), tighter layout

### `ChatMessageViews.kt`
- **Bubble shape**: Directional (flat edge facing sender, rounded opposite)
- **Width**: `0.90f` → `widthIn(max=520dp)` — consistent with ChatScreen
- **Padding**: `11dp/8dp` → `16dp/14dp`
- **Role labels removed** from all bubble variants
- **Tool bubble**: Grouped, compact, expandable (same treatment as ChatScreen)
- **Streaming bubble**: Accent-tinted border instead of full accent border
- **User bubble**: `accentSoft` background, no border (vs old `accent` border)
- **Assistant bubble**: Transparent background, subtle border
- **Code block**: Preserved for syntax highlighting

## Testing

- All exported function signatures preserved (verified against callers in `ChatMessageListCard.kt`, `ChatMarkdown.kt`, and test files)
- `internal` functions (`contextMeterLabel`, `contextMeterThinkingLabel`, `ChatContextUsage`, etc.) preserved for test compatibility
- No new dependencies added
- No gateway API changes
- Brace balance verified

## Before/After

**Before**: 56% bubble width, 3.5dp padding, role labels on every message, tool calls eating 60%+ of screen, error banners blocking chat flow.

**After**: 82% bubble width, 14dp padding, clean bubbles with directional shapes, grouped compact tool indicators, animated thinking dots, errors in header only.

## Notes

- The app README says it is "extremely alpha" and "actively being rebuilt from the ground up" — these are incremental UX improvements within that context
- No skill/provider mutation features included — that would require gateway API verification and is a separate feature request

target.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full
target.body:
## Evidence

**Generated 2026-07-07 from the production `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` function on this branch** using `pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts` (not a test runner — calls the exported production seam directly):

```
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts

=== BEFORE: security unset (fail-closed heuristic active) ===
  BLOCKED: cat bad.py | python
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  BLOCKED: bash -c "python bad.py"
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  PASS: python3 script.py | head -30
    (target path `script.py` extractable → no heuristic, file check runs; passes
     because the file does not exist on this machine)

=== AFTER: security="full" (heuristic bypassed) ===
  ALLOWED: cat bad.py | python
  ALLOWED: bash -c "python bad.py"
  ALLOWED: python3 script.py | head -30
```

The `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` seam is exported from the production module (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`). The proof script imports and calls it directly — no vitest, no mocking, no test infra. `BLOCKED` = the function throws; `ALLOWED` = the function returns `undefined`. Before/after behavior confirmed on the same machine in the same Node.js session.

---

## What Problem This Solves

When `exec.security` is `"full"` and `exec.ask` is `"on-miss"` (a common production config), `shouldSkipExecScriptPreflight` returns `false` because it requires `ask === "off"`. This causes `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` to run the fail-closed interpreter heuristic even though the operator has explicitly declared full agent trust.

The heuristic blocks commands that contain an interpreter invocation + complex shell syntax (pipe, `&&`, etc.) when the script target path cannot be extracted — for example `cat bad.py | python`, `bash -c "python script.py"`, or `python <(cat bad.py)`. In lower-trust configurations this defensive fail-close is the right call. At `security="full"` it produces false positives for patterns like `python3 script.py | head -30` where a pipeline prevents target extraction but the intent is unambiguous.

**Root cause**: `ask` controls approval prompts; `security` controls trust level. These were conflated in the outer skip check, which required `ask === "off"` before any preflight could be bypassed at `security="full"`.

## Fix

Thread `security` into `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` and guard the fail-closed interpreter heuristic behind `security !== "full"`. File content validation (shell variable injection detection via `$VAR` patterns) is **unchanged** — it still runs for all security levels whenever a target path can be extracted from the command.

Changes:
- `validateScriptFileForShellBleed`: add optional `security?: ExecSecurity` param; wrap the interpreter heuristic in `if (params.security !== "full")`
- Call site: pass `security` through
- Tests: add `it.each(failClosedCases)` blocks verifying each previously-blocked command now resolves when `security: "full"` is passed, covering both `ask=on-miss` and `ask=always`
- Docs: update `docs/tools/exec.md` to state `security=full` bypasses the heuristic regardless of ask mode

## Test plan

- [x] All existing `failClosedCases` still fail with default (no `security`) param — heuristic unchanged for non-full security
- [x] All existing `passCases` still pass
- [x] New tests verify each `failClosedCase` resolves when `security: "full"` is passed (covers ask=on-miss and ask=always)
- [x] Existing `createPreflightTool()` tests still catch `$VAR` patterns — file content validation runs regardless of security level

Fixes #87371

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHeartbeatPreflight` in `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` read the workspace `HEARTBEAT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory and processed by the heartbeat pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch to `readRegularFile` with a 16 MiB cap so the read is bounded and rejects symlinks and non-files. This aligns with other bounded-read fixes in the repo and prevents accidental or malicious oversized heartbeat files from causing memory pressure.

## User Impact

Oversized `HEARTBEAT.md` files are now treated like missing files: the heartbeat run continues without the file content. Normal-sized heartbeat files behave exactly as before.

target.title: fix(plugins): remove local dependency denylist
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw plugin installs still carried a built-in, hard-coded local dependency
denylist after ClawHub and operator policy became the intended trust boundaries.
That meant generic local, archive, and npm plugin install paths could be blocked
by OpenClaw's retired local dependency scanner instead of by ClawHub scanning,
`security.installPolicy`, or plugin `before_install` hooks.

## Why This Change Was Made

This removes the built-in local dependency denylist scanner from plugin install
and update validation while preserving the install policy and hook surfaces that
operators and plugins own. ClawHub trust and artifact integrity behavior stay on
the existing ClawHub paths; this PR only removes the hard-coded
dependency-denylist traversal and its package-name checks from OpenClaw install
code.

## User Impact

Plugin installs are no longer rejected solely because a package manifest,
vendored folder, or managed npm dependency tree contains a name from OpenClaw's
former built-in dependency denylist. Operators can still block installs with
`security.installPolicy`, and loaded plugins can still report findings, block
installs, or fail closed through `before_install` hooks.

## Evidence

Reviewer-checkable behavior:

- The net diff deletes `src/plugins/dependency-denylist.ts` and removes its
  traversal/call-site plumbing from plugin install scans.
- Tests now assert that formerly denied `plain-crypto-js` package names are
  allowed in manifests, vendored directories, and managed npm dependency trees
  when no operator policy or hook blocks them.
- Existing hook and policy tests remain in the focused proof to show

target.title: fix: require exact markdown frontmatter delimiters
target.body:
Closes #101769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users writing Markdown command, hook, skill, workshop proposal, or metadata files could have content that starts with non-delimiter text like `---not` or `----` interpreted as YAML frontmatter.

That could make OpenClaw read unexpected metadata and strip or alter body text even though the Markdown did not begin with a whole `---` delimiter line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared markdown-core frontmatter parser now requires exact `---` delimiter lines for both opening and closing fences. Bundled Claude command body extraction and skill workshop proposal stripping now reuse the same shared delimiter extractor instead of keeping separate prefix-based logic.

This keeps metadata parsing and body stripping aligned without adding config, compatibility shims, or plugin-specific policy.

## User Impact

Markdown files can now safely begin with dash-prefixed text that is not a frontmatter delimiter. Valid `---` frontmatter blocks still parse normally, while `---not` and `----` remain part of the Markdown body.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the reported source-level case parsed unexpected metadata:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'EOF'
import { parseFrontmatterBlock } from './packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts';
const content = '---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody';
console.log(JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(content)));
EOF
{"name":"nope"}
```

After the fix, the final source-level proof keeps invalid delimiter text as Markdown and still accepts a valid block:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'EOF'
import { parseFrontmatterBlock, stripFrontmatterBlock } from './packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts';
const invalid = '---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody';
const valid = '---\nname: valid\n---\nbody';
console.log('invalid', JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(invalid)), JSON.stringify(stripFrontmatterBlock(invalid)));
console.log('valid', JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(valid)), JSON.stringify(stripFrontmatterBlock(valid)));
EOF
invalid {} "---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody"
valid {"name":"valid"} "body"
```

Validation run:

```text
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write --threads=1 packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.test.ts src/plugins/bundle-commands.ts src/plugins/bundle-commands.test.ts src/skills/workshop/frontmatter.ts src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(oauth): pass workspace context to resolveProviderIdForAuth on refresh failure
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of the Antigravity AI coding assistant (Gemini 3.5 Flash).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on OAuth token refresh failures.

**Symptom/Behavior:**
When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the global context instead of the workspace-specific configuration. Specifically, `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` is called with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in a failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and a failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L472-L475)` (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block):
```typescript
        const snapshot = getRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(params.agentDir);
        const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider);
        if (snapshot?.lastGood?.[providerKey] === profileId) {
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to pass the full configuration and workspace context to `resolveProviderIdForAuth` during OAuth refresh failure cleanup.

**Solution Overview:**
1. Update `resolveApiKeyForProfile` to accept an optional `workspaceDir` parameter.
2. Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
   ```typescript
   const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
     config: cfg,
     workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir,
   });
   ```
3. Thread the `workspaceDir` context through all calling paths (including `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/model-auth.ts`, and `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts`).

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that when clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected. This prevents stale/broken credentials from sticking around as `lastGood` in workspaces using scoped aliases.

---

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Staged and verified multi-scenario reproduction test suites covering happy path, edge cases, and stress/concurrency scenarios:

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

target.title: fix(heartbeat): bound HEARTBEAT.md file read size
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHeartbeatPreflight` in `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` read the workspace `HEARTBEAT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory and processed by the heartbeat pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch to `readRegularFile` with a 16 MiB cap so the read is bounded and rejects symlinks and non-files. This aligns with other bounded-read fixes in the repo and prevents accidental or malicious oversized heartbeat files from causing memory pressure.

## User Impact

Oversized `HEARTBEAT.md` files are now treated like missing files: the heartbeat run continues without the file content. Normal-sized heartbeat files behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Added `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.oversized-heartbeat-file.test.ts` with a regression test using a `16 MiB + 1` byte file and asserting the run continues.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner.oversized-heartbeat-file.test.ts --run` passes (1/1 tests).

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — sandbox exec-server pipe survival regression test**:

A new test file `sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts` exercises the real
sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge. The test spawns a child process
writing 200 lines to stdout/stderr, kills it mid-output, and verifies the bridge
survives. A second process confirms full functionality. The HTTP streaming path
is also tested with a local echo server.

```text
$ npx vitest run --project extension-codex sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  3.60s

 ✓ process bridge survives when child writes 200 lines then is killed (1234ms)
 ✓ http streaming bridge survives when socket closes mid-stream (570ms)
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

target.title: Add local Claw feed planning
target.body:
## Summary

Stacked after #101328. This adds the first read-only Claw feed layer so OpenClaw can discover a Claw from a feed entry and build the same lifecycle plan introduced in PR2.

- adds `openclaw.clawFeed.v1` types, strict parsing, and local feed file reading
- resolves feed entries to local Claw manifest sources with source-locality checks
- adds owner/trust metadata on feed entries and warnings for missing owner evidence
- adds `openclaw claws feed inspect <feed>` and `openclaw claws feed plan <feed> <claw>`
- keeps PR3 read-only: remote feed fetch, install, mutation, and ClawHub publish/search stay deferred

## Safety / ownership behavior

- relative feed sources must stay under the feed file directory
- absolute local paths are rejected
- remote `http`/`https` sources are rejected in this PR
- `file:` URLs are accepted only if they resolve under the feed directory
- feed entry id must match the resolved manifest id
- feed entry version mismatch is diagnostic-only warning so feeds can surface drift without mutating anything

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/feed.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts src/cli/program/root-command-descriptions.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs`
- `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-claws-pr3-proof-state node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws feed inspect src/claws/fixtures/local-claws.feed.json --json`
- `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-claws-pr3-proof-state node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws feed plan src/claws/fixtures/local-claws.feed.json incident-response --json`
- `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --pretty false --target ES2022 --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --strict --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --types node src/claws/feed.ts src/claws/types.ts src/claws/schema.ts src/claws/plan.ts src/claws/reader.ts src/cli/claws-cli.ts src/cli/claws-cli.runtime.ts`
- `codex review -c model=gpt-5.5 --base origin/user/giodl/claws-pr2-schema-plan` returned no actionable correctness issues after fixing its path-confinement findings.


### Observed real CLI output

`claws feed inspect` against `src/claws/fixtures/local-claws.feed.json`:

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "feed": {
    "id": "local-starter-claws",
    "entries": 1
  },
  "diagnostics": 0
}
```

`claws feed plan` against `src/claws/fixtures/local-claws.feed.json incident-response`:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "openclaw.clawPlan.v1",
  "readOnly": true,
  "claw": {
    "id": "incident-response",
    "name": "Incident Response",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "sourcePath": "/root/src/openclaw-claws-pr3/src/claws/fixtures/incident-response.claw.json"
  },
  "summary": {
    "totalEntries": 5,
    "requiredEntries": 4,
    "optionalEntries": 1,
    "requiresConsent": 2,
    "unsupportedOptionalEntries": 0
  },
  "feed": {
    "id": "local-starter-claws",
    "entry": "incident-response"
  }
}
```

## Notes

I also attempted full-project typecheck paths:

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` could not run because `node_modules/.bin/tsgo` is missing in this worktree.
- direct `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --pretty false` OOMed at the default heap and again with `--max-old-space-size=8192`.

target.title: fix(codex): allow tool-less /btw side questions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex-native /btw currently aborts before forking when the effective tool policy disables native Codex tools, even though /btw can still answer as a lightweight side conversation without tools. That makes harmless side questions fail on restricted sessions.

## Summary

- allow Codex /btw side questions to fork even when the effective tool policy disables the native Codex tool surface
- keep those restricted side threads tool-less by skipping OpenClaw tool bridge construction
- update regression coverage for deny-all and narrow toolsAllow policies

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-support.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- Result: 1 test file passed, 46 tests passed
- `npm test -- --run extensions/codex/index.test.ts`
- Result: 1 test file passed, 10 tests passed
- Local runtime syntax checks passed for the active installed Codex side-question bundles with `node --check`

## Live Restricted /btw Proof

Ran against the real local Codex app-server, not a mocked test client:

- Source commit: `a4dd444efcab358b3d910d75177d7657cb248f96`
- Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.142.5`
- Model: `gpt-5.4-mini`
- Parent thread: started and completed normally
- Side question policy: `toolsAllow: []`
- Side answer: `PROOFOK`
- Old policy abort observed: `false`
- App-server methods observed: `account/login/start`, `thread/start`, `turn/start`, `thread/fork`, `thread/inject_items`, side `turn/start`, `thread/unsubscribe`
- Server tool requests observed: `[]`
- `item/tool/call` request count: `0`
- Approval request count: `0`

Redacted proof excerpt:


target.title: fix(discord): dispose fallback timeout abort listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes fallback abort-signal listener cleanup in the active Discord monitor paths. When native `AbortSignal.any` is unavailable, Discord manually attaches abort listeners to parent signals. The queued message runner and media download path were still using the signal-only helper, so successful monitor work could leave parent signals retaining stale fallback listeners.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback merged signal now has an explicit disposer, and the active Discord monitor callers use it directly:

- `message-run-queue.ts` disposes the merged job/lifecycle abort signal in `finally` after queued processing settles.
- `message-media.ts` disposes the merged request/timeout abort signal in `finally` after media download settles.
- `runDiscordTaskWithTimeout` keeps the same disposable cleanup for the deprecated timeout compatibility path.

## User Impact

Long-running Discord monitor processes avoid accumulating stale abort listeners across repeated queued message runs and media downloads on runtimes or test environments that take the fallback merge path.

## Evidence

- Collision check before opening: no open PR modified `extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.ts` or `extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts`.
- ClawSweeper blocker addressed: the two current signal-only monitor callers it identified are now updated to `createDisposableMergedAbortSignal` and dispose in `finally`.
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-utils.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts --reporter verbose`

Focused test output:

```text
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts > createDiscordMessageHandler queue behavior > disposes fallback run abort listeners after queued processing settles
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-utils.test.ts > resolveMediaList > disposes fallback attachment abort listeners after downloads settle
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts > discord monitor timeouts > disposes fallback merged abort listeners after completed timeout races settle
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts > discord monitor timeouts > does not refire fallback merged abort listeners after timeout races settle

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests  81 passed (81)
```

Representative runtime proof, run with `pnpm exec tsx` against the PR branch, not through Vitest: the harness disables native `AbortSignal.any`, creates a real `createDiscordMessageRunQueue`, enqueues a Discord monitor-style job, captures the abort signal passed to `processDiscordMessage`, then aborts the parent signals after queued processing settles.

```text
Discord monitor queue fallback cleanup proof
{
  "nativeAbortSignalAny": "disabled for fallback path",
  "processed": true,
  "parentAbortListenersAdded": 1,
  "parentAbortListenersRemoved": 1,
  "mergedSignalIsFallback": true,
  "mergedSignalBeforeParentAbort": false,
  "mergedSignalAfterParentAbort": false,
  "runtimeErrorCount": 0
}
```

The regression tests and the runtime proof both force the fallback path by temporarily disabling native `AbortSignal.any`. The runtime proof shows the monitor queue path removed the parent abort listener on normal completion, and aborting the parent signal after settlement no longer aborts the captured merged signal.

target.title: fix: add timeout to parent-fork token count resolution (fixes #101718)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveParentForkTokenCount` reads the parent transcript to estimate token count when forking a session, but has **no timeout or abort signal**. On large transcripts (hundreds of MB) or slow filesystems (NFS, FUSE, saturated SSD), this blocks session creation and reply fork paths indefinitely, accumulating blocked async contexts that exhaust gateway connection slots (#101718).

### Call chain

```
sessions.create({ fork: true })
  → session-create-service resolveParentForkDecision
    → session-fork.ts resolveParentForkTokenCount
      → session-fork.runtime.ts resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime
        (fs.stat + async file read — NO TIMEOUT)
```

## Changes

**2 files, +54/-2 (source: +6; tests: +48)**

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.ts`** (+6 lines):
- Import `withTimeout` from `../../infra/fs-safe.js`
- Add `PARENT_FORK_TOKEN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000` constant
- Wrap `resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime` in `withTimeout(..., 2_000).catch(() => undefined)`

When the 2-second timeout fires, `resolveParentForkTokenCount` returns `undefined` — the same sentinel the normal fallback path already produces. `resolveParentForkDecision` already handles `undefined` correctly: returns `{status: "fork"}` without `parentTokens` estimate.

This single bounded deadline (recommended by ClawSweeper review) covers all filesystem awaits inside the runtime (fs.stat + transcript read up to 1MB + potential index scan) in one wrapper.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts`** (+48 lines):
- 3 new test cases for `resolveParentForkDecision`:
  1. Fast runtime → returns `fork` with `parentTokens` (50k)
  2. **Hanging runtime → returns `fork` without `parentTokens` within 2s** (timeout proof)
  3. Parent too large → returns `skip`

### Why 2 seconds and not 10?
- The timeout only guards the stale-token filesystem probe after the synchronous `freshPersistedTokens` fast path
- Even on NFS, fs.stat + 1MB tail read should complete in < 500ms
- 2s is aggressive but safe: returning `undefined` (allow fork without estimate) is always better than blocking indefinitely

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```

target.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full
target.body:
## Evidence

**Generated 2026-07-07 from the production `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` function on this branch** using `pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts` (not a test runner — calls the exported production seam directly):

```
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts

=== BEFORE: security unset (fail-closed heuristic active) ===
  BLOCKED: cat bad.py | python
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  BLOCKED: bash -c "python bad.py"
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  PASS: python3 script.py | head -30
    (target path `script.py` extractable → no heuristic, file check runs; passes
     because the file does not exist on this machine)

=== AFTER: security="full" (heuristic bypassed) ===
  ALLOWED: cat bad.py | python
  ALLOWED: bash -c "python bad.py"
  ALLOWED: python3 script.py | head -30
```

The `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` seam is exported from the production module (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`). The proof script imports and calls it directly — no vitest, no mocking, no test infra. `BLOCKED` = the function throws; `ALLOWED` = the function returns `undefined`. Before/after behavior confirmed on the same machine in the same Node.js session.

---

## What Problem This Solves

When `exec.security` is `"full"` and `exec.ask` is `"on-miss"` (a common production config), `shouldSkipExecScriptPreflight` returns `false` because it requires `ask === "off"`. This causes `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` to run the fail-closed interpreter heuristic even though the operator has explicitly declared full agent trust.

The heuristic blocks commands that contain an interpreter invocation + complex shell syntax (pipe, `&&`, etc.) when the script target path cannot be extracted — for example `cat bad.py | python`, `bash -c "python script.py"`, or `python <(cat bad.py)`. In lower-trust configurations this defensive fail-close is the right call. At `security="full"` it produces false positives for patterns like `python3 script.py | head -30` where a pipeline prevents target extraction but the intent is unambiguous.

**Root cause**: `ask` controls approval prompts; `security` controls trust level. These were conflated in the outer skip check, which required `ask === "off"` before any preflight could be bypassed at `security="full"`.

## Fix

Thread `security` into `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` and guard the fail-closed interpreter heuristic behind `security !== "full"`. File content validation (shell variable injection detection via `$VAR` patterns) is **unchanged** — it still runs for all security levels whenever a target path can be extracted from the command.

Changes:
- `validateScriptFileForShellBleed`: add optional `security?: ExecSecurity` param; wrap the interpreter heuristic in `if (params.security !== "full")`
- Call site: pass `security` through
- Tests: add `it.each(failClosedCases)` blocks verifying each previously-blocked command now resolves when `security: "full"` is passed, covering both `ask=on-miss` and `ask=always`
- Docs: update `docs/tools/exec.md` to state `security=full` bypasses the heuristic regardless of ask mode

## Test plan

- [x] All existing `failClosedCases` still fail with default (no `security`) param — heuristic unchanged for non-full security
- [x] All existing `passCases` still pass
- [x] New tests verify each `failClosedCase` resolves when `security: "full"` is passed (covers ask=on-miss and ask=always)
- [x] Existing `createPreflightTool()` tests still catch `$VAR` patterns — file content validation runs regardless of security level

Fixes #87371

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Signal setup required users to hand-configure native `signal-cli` even when they wanted OpenClaw to guide them through a local Signal REST container or an existing Signal API server. It also fixes setup/status gaps where Signal transport mode, receive readiness, and multi-account setup state could be misreported or persisted on the wrong account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now owns native, Docker container, and existing-server setup paths inside the Signal plugin, while core setup gains only the generic `setupApplied` rollback signal needed to avoid persisting failed or cancelled setup attempts. Managed Docker setup now verifies the account-specific `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket before saving container setup, so an account-list response alone is not treated as a working Signal setup.

## User Impact

Users can configure Signal through the setup wizard with a Docker container flow, QR/linking guidance, and existing-server reconfiguration that does not require re-entering an already saved Signal number. Operators get clearer `channels status` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states, and mixed multi-account configs keep transport fields scoped to the intended account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Docker setup now verifies `/v1/receive/{account}` before every managed setup success return: single listed account, selected account from multiple linked accounts, and newly linked QR account.
- Non-interactive existing-server setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "auto"` and `autoStart: false`, so a previous container setup does not force a later `--http-url` config through the container adapter.
- Non-interactive native setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "native"`, `autoStart: true`, and clears `httpUrl`, so a later `--cli-path`/host/port setup does not keep using an old external server.
- Failed or cancelled setup returns `setupApplied: false`, so core setup skips account selection hooks, setup callbacks, completion notes, and partial config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts.
- Signal status/probe output now exposes readiness-specific states instead of collapsing account-missing or receive-unavailable probes into generic working/unreachable output.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard and gateway status behavior; the reviewer-checkable proof is the command/test output and config transition coverage below.

Automated checks run on the final target:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/setup-core.test.ts` passed: 2 files, 109 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo` passed.
- `pnpm config:docs:check` passed before the ClawSweeper receive-readiness fix; this fix did not touch generated config docs.
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check` passed before the ClawSweeper receive-readiness fix; this fix did not touch bundled channel metadata.
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` passed before the ClawSweeper receive-readiness fix; this fix did not touch SDK API exports.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- Native review phase: `codex review --base origin/main` returned clean before ClawSweeper requested the receive-readiness hardening.
- Cold review phase: one independent cold review of `origin/main...HEAD` returned no actionable findings before ClawSweeper requested the receive-readiness hardening.
- ClawSweeper iter 1 found the receive-readiness gap; this branch now fixes that finding and adds focused regressions for the three Docker setup success paths.

Safety: this proof did not touch real `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, did not send Signal messages, and did not start arbitrary OpenClaw agents.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |


## Real behavior proof (Docker, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

### Latest fixes

|-------|---------|-----|

| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

### Test results

| Failure-alert (7 tests) | ✅ All passed |

| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |


## Real CLI proof (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway at `885d605e56` running with `--allow-unconfigured`.

**Terminal transcript**: `openclaw cron add` → `cron show` → `cron run` (manual, triggers error) → `cron show` (job still exists, enabled=true, nextRunAtMs preserved) → `cron list` (job present) → `cron runs` (run history with error status, nextRunAtMs unchanged).

| Add job | `openclaw cron add --name proof-job --at ... --delete-after-run` | Created with `deleteAfterRun: true` |
| Manual run | `openclaw cron run <id>` | `{"ok": true, "enqueued": true}` |

## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

| Test | Command | Before (main) | After (PR head) |
|------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| B: every-job manual error | `cron run` → `cron show` | `nextRunAtMs` rewritten by backoff | `nextRunAtMs` unchanged ✅ |
| A+B: counters | `cron runs` | `consecutiveErrors` mutated | Unchanged ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `3d32c9baff`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  - Both `cron show` and `cron list` returned `lastRunWasManual` without schema validation errors, proving `CronJobStateSchema` correctly includes the field ✅

- **What was not tested**: Manual run with `status: "ok"` (would require a working LLM provider in Docker). The `shouldDelete` guard path (`wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual`) is exercised by unit tests. Multi-node cluster, production load.


## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `8596607fca`, 2026-06-02 — backoff fix)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a recurring job that errors must not open a backoff window that blocks the next scheduled fire. Previously, `isErrorBackoffPending()`, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()`, `isPendingErrorBackoffSlot()`, and `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` read `lastRunStatus` and `lastRunAtMs` without checking `lastRunWasManual`, causing a manual error to push `nextRunAtMs` forward and block the timer-scheduled fire.

- **Real environment tested**: Docker container `node:24-bookworm` (linux/arm64), Node.js `v24.16.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`, patched OpenClaw at commit `8596607fca`.

- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` does not check `lastRunWasManual`. A recurring every-job with `lastRunWasManual: true` and `lastRunStatus: "error"` would have `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` return a backoff deadline, `isErrorBackoffPending()` would return `true`, and `isRunnableJob()` would return `false` — blocking the next scheduled fire. `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` would also push `nextRunAtMs` forward to the backoff floor. Test file authored as part of this PR.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
  -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app \
  -e NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=8192" -e CI=true \
  node:24-bookworm bash -c \
  "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts \
    src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts \
    src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts"

# Live Gateway CLI in Docker
docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 \
  -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app \
  -e NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=8192" -e CI=true \
  -e OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test \
  -e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=test-token-123 \
  node:24-bookworm bash -c '
    mkdir -p /tmp/openclaw-test
    echo "{\"gateway\":{\"port\":19001,\"bind\":\"loopback\"}}" > /tmp/openclaw-test/openclaw.json
    node openclaw.mjs gateway run --dev --allow-unconfigured --token test-token-123 --port 19001 &
    sleep 8
    node openclaw.mjs cron add --name test-at-delete --at "2026-06-02T23:00:00Z" --message reminder --delete-after-run --url ws://127.0.0.1:19001 --token test-token-123
    # extract ID, then: cron run <ID>, cron show <ID>, cron list
    node openclaw.mjs cron add --name test-recurring --every 10s --message "recurring check" --url ws://127.0.0.1:19001 --token test-token-123
    # extract ID, then: cron run <ID>, cron show <ID>
    kill %1'
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. **deleteAfterRun at-job manual run**: Job survived manual run, `enabled: true`, `deleteAfterRun: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅
  2. **Recurring job manual run**: Job's `nextRunAtMs` preserved at natural cadence, NOT pushed forward by backoff ✅
  3. **Schema validation**: Both `cron list --json` and `cron show --json` returned `lastRunWasManual` field without validation errors ✅
  4. **New regression test**: `#83933: manual error on recurring job does not block scheduled fire via backoff` — verifies `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` returns `undefined` for manual errors, `isRunnableJob()` returns `true` within theoretical backoff window, `recomputeNextRunsForMaintenance()` computes natural cadence (not backoff floor), and control case confirms scheduled errors still apply backoff ✅

- **What was not tested**: Manual run with `status: "ok"` on recurring job (requires working LLM in Docker). Multi-node cluster, production load, actual delivery to chat channels.




## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: With the guard disabled (`false && opts?.isManual`), the new regression test fails — a manual ok run rewrites `nextRunAtMs` to the natural next fire (`endedAt + 60s`) instead of preserving the pending backoff window (`endedAt + 30min`), while the other regression tests still pass. Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. When manual, `nextRunAtMs` is left untouched (with an info log). When not manual, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (naturalNext computation, cron `MIN_REFIRE_GAP_MS` safety net via `resolveCronNextRunWithLowerBound`, every-schedule path). The disabled-job terminal `else { job.state.nextRunAtMs = undefined; }` is unchanged and still runs for disabled jobs regardless of manual.
- **Exact steps run after patch**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```
 ✓ cron src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (81 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  81 passed (81)
```
oxlint → 0 warnings, 0 errors. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` → exit 0. oxfmt --check → all files correctly formatted.

- **New regression test**: `#83538: manual ok run on recurring job preserves pending scheduled error-backoff window` — sets up an `every` 60s job with a pending backoff window (`nextRunAtMs = endedAt + 30min`, `consecutiveErrors: 2`), runs a manual OK completion (`isManual: true`), and asserts the backoff `nextRunAtMs` is preserved (not reset to the natural next run). The job stays enabled with counter intact.
- **Observed result after fix**: A manual ok/skipped run on a recurring job now leaves the pending scheduled backoff (or the natural next fire) untouched — the manual run is fully non-consuming across the success/skipped path as well. Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI end-to-end for this specific success-path branch (a manual `ok` outcome requires a working LLM provider in Docker; earlier Docker CLI proofs cover the manual-run survival/backoff paths). Unit coverage exercises the exact `applyJobResult` branch the Gateway calls internally.

target.title: fix(reply): preserve routed transcript mirror metadata
target.body:
## Summary

- Preserves full `sourceReplyTranscriptMirror` metadata when final replies are routed through `routeReply`, instead of collapsing that mirror state down to the minimal outbound shape.
- Extends outbound transcript mirroring so `expectedSessionId`, `storePath`, and `deliveryMirror` survive durable delivery and reach transcript append.
- Rebases on latest `upstream/main` while keeping current reply-completion and outbound-recovery behavior intact.
- Adds regression coverage across the routed reply caller path, the `routeReply` boundary, and the outbound transcript append boundary so future reply-routing changes do not silently drop transcript binding metadata.

## Linked context

Related #92489

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:**
  Routed final replies were dropping source-reply transcript mirror metadata before transcript append, so `expectedSessionId`, `storePath`, or `deliveryMirror` could be lost across outbound delivery.

- **Real environment tested:**
  Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS, rebased on latest `upstream/main`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts -t "mirror metadata"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts -t "passes source reply transcript mirror"
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
route-reply + deliver mirror metadata tests
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  2 passed | 175 skipped (177)

dispatch-from-config routed mirror test
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  1 passed | 254 skipped (255)
  passes source reply transcript mirror through routed final delivery
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  Routed finals with `sourceReplyTranscriptMirror` pass the full mirror object into `routeReply`; outbound delivery forwards `expectedSessionId`, `storePath`, and `deliveryMirror` to transcript append; ordinary routed finals without source metadata keep default mirroring (`mirror` left undefined, not `false`).

- **What was not tested:**
  No live Slack/Telegram end-to-end run or transcript readback from a real channel account; no committed proof scripts.

## Review status

- Rebased on latest `upstream/main` (includes #99549 reply-completion and #99600 outbound-recovery fixes).
- Ready for `@clawsweeper re-review`.

target.title: docs(cli): clarify that exec-policy show and approvals get exclude per-session /exec overrides
target.body:
<!-- PR TITLE -->
docs(cli): clarify that exec-policy show and approvals get exclude per-session /exec overrides

<!-- PR BODY -->

## What Problem This Solves

Running `openclaw exec-policy show` or `openclaw approvals get` to inspect effective exec policy shows config + host approvals state, but **not** per-session `/exec` overrides set in an active chat or cron session. Nothing in the CLI output or docs mentioned this gap. A user who had set `/exec security=full ask=off` in a session and then ran `exec-policy show` would see a different policy than what was actually in use, with no hint about why.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Both `exec-policy show` and `approvals get` build output from the config snapshot and host approvals file only — session state is never loaded in either path.
- The existing `effectivePolicy.note` field is already rendered in both human-readable and `--json` output, so appending the caveat there is the minimal correct fix with no new surface.
- `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md`, `docs/cli/approvals.md`, and `docs/tools/permission-modes.md` all describe these commands without mentioning the session override gap; a `<Note>` block in each keeps the docs aligned with CLI output.

**Scope note:** this PR is a diagnostic clarification only. The underlying runtime issue — `SYSTEM_RUN_DISABLED` despite effective policy showing `security=full` — is tracked separately in #79983 and requires a different fix path. Merging this should not close or de-prioritize that issue.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw exec-policy show` or `openclaw approvals get` now see the following appended to the policy note in both text and `--json` output:

```
Per-session /exec overrides are not included; send /exec in the target chat or cron session to inspect them.
```

Docs pages for exec approvals, approvals CLI, and permission modes carry a matching `<Note>` block.

No config, approval logic, or enforcement behavior is changed. No migration required.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts`
  - `Test Files  2 passed (2)`
  - `Tests  30 passed (30)`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:**
  CLI diagnostics for `exec-policy show` and `approvals get` now warn that per-session `/exec` overrides are excluded, and docs match that caveat.

- **Real environment tested:**
  Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with fresh temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, rebased on latest `upstream/main`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$tmpdir"

pnpm openclaw exec-policy preset yolo --json
pnpm openclaw exec-policy show --json
pnpm openclaw approvals get --json
pnpm openclaw approvals get
```

Session inspection path reference (no live chat required):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.exec-hint.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

`exec-policy show --json` / `approvals get --json` note excerpt:

```text
Per-session /exec overrides are not included; send /exec in the target chat or cron session to inspect them.
```

`approvals get` text excerpt:

```text
Precedence: Effective exec policy is the host approvals file intersected with requested tools.exec policy. Per-session /exec overrides are not included; send /exec in the target chat or cron session to inspect them.
```

Session-status hint contract (Vitest):

```text
Current session exec defaults: host=gateway security=full ask=always node=worker-1.
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  Both CLI commands append the session caveat in JSON and text output; docs carry matching `<Note>` blocks; focused CLI tests pass.

- **What was not tested:**
  No live chat `/exec` command in Telegram/Discord; no committed proof scripts.

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

Nostr has two user-visible reply paths: the shared outbound adapter and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback. Both could forward raw assistant text before this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nostr outbound adapter lacked a `sanitizeText` hook, and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback sent `convertMarkdownTables(outboundText)` directly via `reply`, bypassing any channel sanitizer. Core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` does not remove tool-trace failure banners.

This adds `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on:
1. `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` (shared outbound delivery path)
2. the inbound DM `deliver` callback before markdown table conversion (the main bot-reply path for incoming Nostr DMs)

This matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, LINE, and Nextcloud Talk.

## User Impact

Nostr users no longer see internal tool-trace failure banners in bot replies on either outbound delivery or inbound DM replies. Normal assistant prose and markdown table conversion behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

**Negative control — core strip keeps banner (pre-fix behavior):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding } from "./src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text)));
console.log("Banner survives:", stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text).includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
Banner survives: true
```

**After fix — outbound adapter hook strips banner:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { nostrPlugin } from "./extensions/nostr/src/channel.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
const result = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } });
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(result));
console.log("Banner stripped:", !result?.includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done."
Banner stripped: true
```

**Inbound DM reply path — gateway harness strips banner before relay reply:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts --run -t "strips internal tool-trace"

 ✓ nostr inbound gateway path
   ✓ strips internal tool-trace banners before inbound DM replies

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 2 skipped (3)
```

The test drives the real gateway `onMessage` → `deliver` callback boundary and asserts the relay `reply` receives `converted:Done.` (sanitized before `convertMarkdownTables`), not the raw tool-trace banner.

**Outbound adapter regression:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Lint (changed files):**

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/nostr/src/gateway.ts extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts extensions/nostr/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts

(no findings)
```

Verified on branch `fix/nostr-sanitize-outbound-90684` at `b2a1bcec0d1`.

**What was not tested:** No live Nostr relay round-trip — credentials were not available in this checkout. The bug is in the sanitization layer before network delivery; the focused gateway harness test exercises the inbound reply path that previously bypassed the outbound adapter hook.

AI-assisted: Cursor (Claude). Proof run manually.

Sibling references: #101708 (LINE), #101712 (Nextcloud Talk), merged #98705 (Feishu).

target.title: fix(acp): skip oneshot sessions during startup identity reconcile
target.body:
Fixes #72013

## Summary

Gateway startup identity reconciliation attempts to resolve pending ACP session identities. Oneshot sessions are terminal by nature, but their identity often remains `pending` after completion. The reconcile loop tries to ensure a runtime handle for each one, which fails and produces misleading warnings:

```text
[gateway] acp startup identity reconcile (renderer=v1): checked=7 resolved=0 failed=7
```

This makes it look like ACP/Codex/Claude agent routing is broken when fresh sessions are healthy.

## Fix

Skip sessions with `mode === "oneshot"` in `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` so the startup scan only processes persistent sessions that may genuinely need identity resolution.

## Changed files

- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.ts` -- Added `session.acp.mode === "oneshot"` guard after the session key check
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.test.ts` -- Regression test: oneshot session with pending identity is skipped (checked=0, no ensure/getStatus calls)
- `scripts/prove-acp-startup-oneshot-list-visible.ts` -- Production-path proof: session-store-visible `listAcpSessionEntries` + reconcile eligibility

## Overlap with #85399

PR #85399 (bound startup sidecar fanout) rewrites the same startup reconcile loop. This PR's guard (`session.acp.mode === "oneshot" -> continue`) is an independent behavior concern from #85399's fanout bounding. Both changes apply cleanly on the same function. Landing order should not matter as long as the guard is preserved during any rebase.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Startup identity reconcile must not process store-visible oneshot ACP rows that still have pending identity + stable `acpxSessionId`, while persistent pending rows remain eligible.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node from workspace toolchain, OpenClaw PR branch `fix/acp-reconcile-skip-oneshot` at commit after proof script add, using **production** `listAcpSessionEntries` + `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` (not a reimplemented loop).
- **Why SQLite-only proof is insufficient:** `listAcpSessionEntries` joins SQLite `acp_sessions` rows to a readable session-store entry and **drops** rows without a matching store entry (`session-meta.ts`). This proof seeds **both** the JSON session store and SQLite via production `upsertAcpSessionMeta`, then prints direct list output.
- **Exact command run after this patch:**

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx scripts/prove-acp-startup-oneshot-list-visible.ts
```

- **Evidence (redacted paths are machine temp dirs; no secrets):**

```console
PROOF_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj
STORE_PATH=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj/sessions/main.json
DATABASE_PATH=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj/state/openclaw.sqlite
LIST_ACP_SESSION_ENTRIES_COUNT=2
LIST_ROW sessionKey=agent:main:acp:oneshot-proof-visible mode=oneshot state=idle identityState=pending hasAcpxSessionId=true storeSessionId=sess-oneshot-proof
LIST_ROW sessionKey=agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible mode=persistent state=idle identityState=pending hasAcpxSessionId=true storeSessionId=eeeedc2b-ead9-40e5-b40e-71fa768ecf19
ONESHOT_STORE_VISIBLE=true
PERSISTENT_STORE_VISIBLE=true
RECONCILE_ELIGIBLE_CALL sessionKey=agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible mode=persistent
RECONCILE_RESULT checked=1 resolved=0 failed=0
ENSURE_CALLS=["agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible"]
ONESHOT_ENSURE_SKIPPED=true
PERSISTENT_ENSURE_CALLED=true
PROOF_OK

```

Interpretation:
- `LIST_ACP_SESSION_ENTRIES_COUNT=2` with both `ONESHOT_STORE_VISIBLE=true` and `PERSISTENT_STORE_VISIBLE=true` shows the startup scan input path sees both rows (the ClawSweeper gap from SQLite-only injection).
- `RECONCILE_RESULT checked=1` with `ONESHOT_ENSURE_SKIPPED=true` and `PERSISTENT_ENSURE_CALLED=true` shows oneshot is skipped while the persistent pending stable row remains reconcile-eligible.

## Tests

- Unit regression in `manager.startup-identity-reconcile.test.ts` for oneshot skip semantics.
- Production-module prove script above for store-visible list + eligibility.
