target.title: fix(session-memory): bound session transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getRecentSessionContent` in `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the session-memory extraction path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session-memory extraction now uses a bounded hybrid reader:
- For transcripts that fit under the 16 MiB cap, it streams lines newest-first through the shared `streamSessionTranscriptLinesReverse` helper and stops before retaining a line that would cross the cap.
- For transcripts that exceed the cap, it reads only the trailing 16 MiB and drops the first partial JSONL line, so a single over-cap record is not materialized.

This avoids whole-file buffering while preserving recent session context.

## User Impact

Session-memory extraction now safely bounds oversized transcripts while still keeping the most recent messages available for context.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests covering:
  - a transcript exceeding the cap with recent trailing messages — asserts the recent messages are preserved and the huge early message is absent,
  - a single JSONL row larger than the cap — asserts `getRecentSessionContent` returns `null`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.test.ts --run` passes (5/5 tests).

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the actual changed helper from source and exercises both the oversized-tail path and the lone over-cap row path.

Script: `/tmp/proof-101475.mjs` (not committed).

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101475.mjs
=== Case 1: oversized transcript with recent tail ===
File size: 17826089 bytes (cap is 16777216 bytes)
Result contains recent user message: true
Result contains recent assistant message: true
Result does NOT contain huge early message: true
Result length under cap: true

=== Case 2: lone over-cap JSONL row ===
Result is null: true
```

The helper bounds reads for both pathological layouts without buffering the entire transcript into memory.

target.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related gaps in `openclaw security audit` where operators could miss high-impact exposure on open chat surfaces and extension plugin command entry points.

### Gap 1: Control-plane tools on open inbound policy

When a channel uses `groupPolicy="open"` or an open DM policy, the exposure matrix flagged elevated and runtime/filesystem tools but did **not** separately flag **control-plane tools** (`cron`, `gateway`).

### Gap 2: Extension plugin commands on chat command surfaces

The plugin trust audit did not evaluate native command surfaces separately, name affected channels in finding detail, or warn when enabled extension plugins register commands reachable on those surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Control-plane exposure:** `collectRiskyToolExposureContexts()` now probes `cron` and `gateway`. Emits `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` (critical) when open inbound policy can reach control-plane tools.

**Plugin command surface audit:** `collectPluginsTrustFindings()` adds `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()` and new/updated findings:

| checkId | After |
|---|---|
| `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` | critical when native commands **or** skill commands enabled without `plugins.allow`; detail names channels |
| `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | warn when enabled extensions register commands and native commands are configured |

**Docs:** `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` uses the correct `plugins.allow` config key.

## User Impact

* Operators get clearer findings when open chats can reach gateway/cron control or extension plugin commands.
* `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` may now report `critical` when native commands are active without `plugins.allow`.
* No runtime behavior change.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts \
  src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Open inbound policy could expose gateway/cron control-plane tools and plugin command surfaces without dedicated audit findings.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin arm64), Node.js v22.22.0, local source checkout on branch `codex/audit-plugin-command-control-surface` (single commit on latest `main`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ security audit trust model findings > evaluates trust-model exposure findings
   (includes security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane scenarios)
 ✓ security audit install metadata findings > evaluates install metadata findings
   (includes plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface scenarios)

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Production collectors `collectExposureMatrixFindings` and `collectPluginsTrustFindings` emit `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` for open group + coding profile setups and `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` when enabled extensions register commands on configured native command surfaces.
- **What was not tested:** Full `openclaw security audit --deep` CLI against a live gateway; no committed `scripts/proof-*.mjs` helpers. Control-plane check ID overlaps with [#100965](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100965) — maintainers should pick one canonical contract.

target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract.

- Removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, registrations, dependencies, private runtime/catalog, Matrix-only artifacts, and standalone release orchestration.
- Keeps `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` only as a thin QA Lab selector for the shared scenario/profile host and `live:matrix` adapter.
- Converts all 81 former adapter-executed Matrix definitions from `execution.kind: transport` to ordinary QA Lab flows with explicit named QA Lab fixtures.
- Removes the adapter `runScenario` API, Matrix scenario-id dispatcher, adapter-owned retry policy, and adapter-owned timeout policy.
- Keeps scenario selection, sequencing, retries, timeouts, assertions, artifacts, and failure reporting in QA Lab. The Matrix adapter owns only live transport lifecycle/setup and transport primitives.
- Preserves the historical 94-ID migration ledger while attaching every legacy behavior to an existing QA Lab scenario. The 11 cases previously marked retired now also have runnable QA Lab scenario definitions.

No compatibility fallback is retained because it would recreate a second Matrix execution path.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation and evidence format.

- `qa matrix --profile release` remains the focused two-scenario release selector.
- `qa matrix --profile fast` retains 11 scenarios.
- `qa matrix --profile transport` retains 50 scenarios.
- Media and E2EE profiles retain their previous membership.
- `qa matrix` / `--profile all` retains the 92-scenario default profile, with two legacy explicit-only scenarios still excluded from the default exactly as before.
- Per-scenario provider mode, Matrix config, retry count, timeout, artifacts, and failure semantics are preserved.

There is no shipped Matrix channel runtime change. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

- Dependency/base proof:
  - Rebased onto `origin/main` `3d206140f3f0ab639cebb67fa20c93c15296c61f`.
  - PR #101055 is merged and its channel-driver lifecycle seam remains the only live Matrix lifecycle path.
- Migration parity:
  - All 81 former `kind: transport` definitions are now `kind: flow` and bind to unique named QA Lab fixtures.
  - Mechanical comparison against the pre-refactor definitions found 0 mismatches across channel, provider mode, Matrix config, retry count, and timeout.
  - Profile assertions: `all=92`, `fast=11`, `release=2`, `transport=50`, `media=7`, `e2ee-smoke=8`, `e2ee-deep=18`, `e2ee-cli=9`.
  - The 94-entry legacy ledger has no missing or duplicate IDs, and every entry resolves to a QA Lab scenario.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox: `tbx_01kwyj4z2n1y4msce7qajwdavb` (`golden-hermit`):
  - SDK + QA Lab focused proof: 125 tests passed.
  - Matrix observer/topology follow-up: 29 tests passed.
  - `check:test-types` passed.
  - Targeted oxlint and `git diff --check` passed.
- Review:
  - Final branch autoreview found and prompted a real fix for rooms that exclude the driver account; the adapter now observes each room with a joined non-SUT account.
  - Fresh final whole-branch Codex autoreview on `e7ad52ae49ec6eab851ff850d48aa263e27e404c`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact-target release proof dispatched:
  - Focused `qa-live-matrix`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28879900596
  - Full manual QA Live: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28879902435

target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution already emits diagnostics when a configured SecretRef fails and provider env credentials are used instead, but `openclaw security audit` and doctor did not surface that boundary drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a config-layer plugin load path collector that reuses existing discovery and doctor bundled-path helpers, then maps results to structured security audit findings (`plugins.load_paths.*`). Added a shared secrets diagnostic helper (`collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics`) used by both security audit (`secrets.ref_env_fallback_used`) and a new doctor health check (`core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback`). Deep skill code-safety scan retains `includeArchived: true`.

## User Impact

* Operators running `openclaw security audit` now get early warnings when `plugins.load.paths` points at risky or missing locations, and when configured SecretRefs silently fall back to env credentials.
* `openclaw doctor` now emits structured warnings for SecretRef env fallback cases that previously only appeared in runtime/gateway logs.
* No config schema, runtime enforcement, or secret resolution behavior changes.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts \
  src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts \
  src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Security audit and doctor did not surface risky `plugins.load.paths` entries or SecretRef env-fallback boundary drift.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin arm64), Node.js v22.22.0, local source checkout on branch `codex/audit-load-paths-secretref-fallback` (single commit on latest `main`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  2. Programmatic doctor health-check detect via production `CORE_HEALTH_CHECKS` entry `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` (same code path as `openclaw doctor` Gateway auth contribution)
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ flags world-writable configured plugin load paths
 ✓ flags missing configured plugin load paths
 ✓ maps shared diagnostics to a security audit finding
 ✓ flags gateway token SecretRef env fallback
 ✓ skips gateway token fallback when auth mode is password

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  8 passed (8)

[warning] core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback: gateway.auth.token SecretRef could not be resolved; runtime is using OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN env fallback.
doctor findings: 1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Audit collectors emit `plugins.load_paths.*` and `secrets.ref_env_fallback_used`; the doctor health check `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` (wired under `doctor:gateway-auth`) surfaces the same shared diagnostic as a warning.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway startup with real SecretRef providers; no committed `scripts/proof-*.mjs` helpers.

## AI-assisted disclosure

- AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- Human-directed scope and review of audit/doctor wiring

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes garbled verbose inbound previews in Mattermost when message bodies contain emoji or other astral characters near the 200-character preview limit. Raw `slice(0, 200)` could split UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing lone surrogates in gateway debug logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaces `bodyText.slice(0, 200)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(bodyText, 200)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` in the verbose inbound preview path.

## User Impact

Operators enabling verbose Mattermost inbound logging see clean previews on emoji boundaries. No change to message delivery or agent-visible content.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Verbose inbound preview could split emoji astral characters at the 200-code-unit boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin arm64), Node.js v22.22.0, local source checkout on branch `fix/mattermost-monitor-utf16-truncation`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ keeps verbose inbound previews on complete UTF-16 boundaries

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** A 199-ASCII + emoji + tail message produces preview `"aaa…aaa"` (199 `a` chars) with no split surrogate; verbose debug line matches production monitor path.
- **What was not tested:** Live Mattermost websocket connection against a remote server.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded in-process Maps across Mattermost monitor and outbound paths:

1. **Monitor channel/user caches** — per-monitor lookups with TTL but no size cap.
2. **Outbound send caches** — bot user, user-by-name, channel-by-name, and DM channel caches.
3. **Opaque target cache** — ID-shaped target resolution cache with no eviction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applies `pruneMapToMaxSize` via shared cache-write helpers: monitor caches capped at **1 000**, outbound bot-user cache at **256**, other outbound/opaque caches at **1 024**.

## User Impact

Long-lived Mattermost gateways get bounded memory for monitor and outbound resolution caches. Normal workloads below the caps are unchanged.

target.title: fix(infra): log restart sentinel cleanup errors instead of silent catch
target.body:
## Summary

- 将 `clearRestartSentinel()` 和 `removeLegacyRestartSentinel()` 中的空 `catch {}` 改为记录错误
- 空 catch 块会静默吞噬数据库写入和文件删除的失败，导致过期 sentinel 标记遗留在数据库中
- 下次重启时可能错误触发意外的恢复流程

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** 两个 try-catch 块使用空 catch 吞噬了所有异常，使开发者无法发现清理 restart sentinel 时发生的错误。

**Real environment tested:** 本地 Linux 环境 (Node 22.21.0, SQLite)，通过强制破坏 SQLite 数据库和文件系统结构来触发清理失败路径。

**Scenario 1: SQLite 数据库损坏**
```
[openclaw] Failed to clear restart sentinel: Error: file is not a database
    at configureSqliteWalMaintenance (.../src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts:327:6)
    at configureSqliteConnectionPragmas (.../src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts:375:23)
    at openOpenClawStateDatabase (.../src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts:935:21)
    at runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction (.../src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts:961:20)
    at clearRestartSentinel (.../src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts:215:5)
    ...
}
```
修复前：此异常被 `catch {}` 静默吞噬，无任何输出。
修复后：错误信息和堆栈完整打印到 stderr。

**Scenario 2: State 目录被替换为文件（双重失败路径）**
```
[openclaw] Failed to clear restart sentinel: Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory
[openclaw] Failed to remove legacy restart sentinel: [Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory]
```
修复前：两条错误均被静默吞噬。
修复后：DB 清理和旧版文件清理的失败路径均独立打印错误日志。

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
使用 tsx 脚本强制破坏 SQLite 数据库和文件系统，直接调用 clearRestartSentinel() 触发真实错误。

**Evidence after fix:**
- 27 个现有单元测试全部通过
- 强制触发两种不同的清理失败场景，均正确输出 `[openclaw] Failed to ...` 日志

**What was not tested:**
- 未在生产环境 (Gateway) 中验证错误恢复流程
- console.error 的副作用本身不在单元测试中断言（但通过手动脚本确认了行为）

## Tests and validation

所有 27 个现有测试通过，未改动测试文件。

验证命令:
```
pnpm test src/infra/restart-sentinel.test.ts
```

## Risk checklist

- User-facing behavior change? → No, 仅增加日志输出
- Config/default surface change? → No
- Security-sensitive change? → No
- Compatibility concern? → No

AI-assisted: 使用 Claude Code 编写此修复。

target.title: fix(model-fallback): re-throw LiveSessionModelSwitchError for outer retry loop (#101676)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user changes the model mid-turn (via `/model`, session_status model override, or cron job override) while the AI is actively generating a response, the run terminates with an error instead of retrying the turn against the newly-selected model.

**Evidence from the issue (#101676):**
```
info: live session model switch requested: claude-sonnet-5 -> claude-sonnet-4-6
warn: model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed ... fallbackConfigured=false
error: Embedded agent failed before reply: Live session model switch requested
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The `runWithModelFallback` loop catches `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` from the embedded runner. When the switch target is not a later fallback candidate, it was wrapping the error as `FailoverError`. With no fallbacks configured, this reached `throwFallbackFailureSummary` producing `FallbackSummaryError` — not `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` — so the outer retry loop never caught it.

**Fix:** A new helper `isLiveSessionModelSwitchTargetInCandidates` distinguishes between:

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Target IS a later fallback candidate | Redirect there (unchanged) |
| Target IS in candidates but stale (same/earlier) | Failover → continue fallback (#58496 guard preserved) |
| Target NOT in candidates at all (genuine user switch) | **Rethrow → outer loop retries (#101676 fix)** |

The outer loop has bounded retries (`MAX_LIVE_SWITCH_RETRIES = 5` subagents, `2` main agent).

## Evidence

### Focused Tests — Three Control-Flow Branches

```
 ✓ re-throws LiveSessionModelSwitchError when the switch target is not a configured candidate (#101676)
```

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path (`sandbox-exec-server/http.ts`) had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178` and other sibling spawn paths: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Before / after (processes.ts)**:

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Before / after (http.ts)**:

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — real sandbox exec-server WebSocket bridge**:

Both paths exercised through the production sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge. A child process writing 200 lines each to stdout/stderr is terminated mid-output; the bridge survives and a second process starts normally. The streaming HTTP subprocess path also survives socket closure mid-stream without crashing.

```text

[14:53:42] EXEC-SERVER: WebSocket connected
```

target.title: fix(feishu): add video preview covers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw sends outbound Feishu videos as `msg_type=media` with only `{ file_key }`. Feishu's message-content docs say video `media` messages can also include an optional `image_key` for the cover image; when OpenClaw omits it, video bubbles can render without a preview frame.

Docs: https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/im-v1/message-content-description/create_json?lang=zh-CN

## Summary
- Generate a JPEG preview frame for outbound Feishu video messages and upload it with the existing image upload API.
- Include the returned `image_key` alongside `file_key` for `msg_type=media`, matching Feishu's documented video content shape.
- Keep the preview best-effort: if frame extraction or preview upload fails, the video still sends with the existing `{ file_key }` payload.
- Bound preview extraction with a short 5s ffmpeg timeout so failed covers do not stall outbound video delivery.

## Evidence
- `git diff --check`
- `/Users/l/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin/pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/feishu/src/media.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
- `/Users/l/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin/pnpm exec node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` (45 tests passed)
- `/Users/l/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin/pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`
- `/Users/l/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin/pnpm lint:extensions`
- Full local `pnpm check:test-types` and `pnpm lint --threads=8` still hit unrelated pre-existing `src/gateway/server-cron*.test.ts` core errors; the extension-specific type/lint checks above pass for this PR's touched files.
- Live Feishu send with the branch succeeded for a 5-second mp4. A `message.get` readback returned `code=0`, `msgType=media`, and confirmed the sent content contains both `file_key` and `image_key` without logging the private keys.
- Screenshot proof: the lower video bubble renders the generated preview frame; the upper gray bubble is a no-preview comparison. Duration display is intentionally out of scope for this PR and is covered separately by #98235.

![Feishu video preview proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/areslp/openclaw/codex/pr-98458-feishu-preview-proof/pr-evidence/feishu-video-preview-cover.jpg)

- The first live attempt exposed ffmpeg's safe-output `.part` suffix handling; the implementation explicitly uses `-c:v mjpeg -f image2` instead of relying on the output filename extension.

target.title: fix(qa): reuse cached image for web search smoke lane
target.body:
Related: #97340

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where QA Smoke CI could spend the entire scenario budget rebuilding the `openai-web-search-minimal` Docker image when running the native web_search smoke wrapper, causing the scenario to time out before reaching the assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QA Docker lane wrapper now matches the regular Docker E2E plan for `openai-web-search-minimal` by defaulting `OPENCLAW_SKIP_DOCKER_BUILD` to `1` for that lane. The overlay still respects an explicit caller override, so maintainers can force a rebuild with `OPENCLAW_SKIP_DOCKER_BUILD=0` when needed.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Operators and maintainers should get a faster, less flaky QA smoke wrapper for the OpenAI native web_search scenario when a cached E2E image is already available.

## Evidence

- Before fix: in the #97340 QA Smoke CI artifact `qa-smoke-profile-telegram-2-of-2-28861430386-1`, `OpenAI native web_search request assertions` failed with `node timed out after 1800000ms`; the scenario log repeatedly reported `Docker build openai-web-search-minimal-build still running`.
- After fix: PR #101651 `QA Smoke CI (telegram 2/2)` passed on head `a81b4b6a64be132bbb49fdc073fa9d6498db7675`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28865855712/job/85615734409
- After-fix artifact: `qa-smoke-profile-telegram-2-of-2-28865855712-1` shows `OpenAI native web_search request assertions` with `status: pass` and the same wrapper path, `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`.
- After-fix scenario log excerpt:

```text
$ node --import tsx test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts --lane openai-web-search-minimal
Reusing Docker image: openclaw-openai-web-search-minimal-e2e
```

target.title: fix(agents): add lock release timeout on attempt teardown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run fails abnormally during tool execution (e.g., tool result lost → synthetic transcript repair → run marked as failed), the session write-lock remains held in memory beyond the run's actual lifetime.

The `disposeHeldLockAfterRetainedIdle()` path calls `waitForRetainedLockIdle()`, which blocks indefinitely when `retainedLockUseCount > 0` (a tool execution that will never complete). The `finally` block in `attempt.ts` hangs at `releaseRetainedSessionLock()`, so the lock is never released. The watchdog eventually reclaims it, but only after the full configured `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes for a 15-minute agent timeout).

During this entire window, **all subsequent requests to the same session fail** with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError` (60s acquire timeout), even though the owning run is no longer active.

### Observed behavior

```
session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=72859
```

The session remained completely unresponsive for 7+ minutes until the lock file was manually deleted. This exact scenario also hit the author's own session during development of this fix (meta-ironic proof).

## Why This Change Was Made

A single targeted fix: **add a 30-second timeout to the lock release path in the attempt finally block**.

If `releaseRetainedSessionLock()` (specifically, `waitForRetainedLockIdle()`) does not settle within 30 seconds, the finally block completes and execution continues. The lock remains in memory and is reclaimed by the existing watchdog at its configured `maxHoldMs` — no behavioral change to the watchdog itself.

Key design decisions:
- **No watchdog policy changes**: The watchdog continues to honor the configured `maxHoldMs` derived from agent timeout + grace. Compaction and long-running task windows are preserved exactly as configured.
- **Timer hygiene**: The timeout is extracted into a focused helper (`attempt.release-lock-timeout.ts`) that uses `.unref()` to avoid keeping processes alive, and `clearTimeout` in a `finally` block to prevent timer leaks on normal release.
- **Minimal blast radius**: Only the attempt teardown path is affected. Normal runs that release promptly never see the timeout.

## User Impact

Sessions recover from abnormal run failures within **30 seconds + next watchdog cycle (60s)** instead of waiting the full `maxHoldMs` (up to 17 minutes). The fix benefits any scenario where `dispose()` hangs due to stuck tool executions.

## Evidence

**Root cause trace (from real production incident):**
1. Agent run executing `exec` tool → command not found → tool result lost
2. Synthetic error result injected for transcript repair
3. Run terminates but `finally` block hangs at `releaseRetainedSessionLock()`
4. Lock still in `SESSION_LOCKS.heldEntries()` → `heldByThisProcess = true` → orphan-self-pid skipped
5. Watchdog threshold = 17 minutes → session blocked for entire duration

**Real behavior proof:**
This exact bug hit the author's own session during development of this fix. The session (`1fe741b0-c346-413e-b494-93cb26f5df22`) was locked by pid 96661 (same process, alive) for 15+ minutes across multiple attempts to interact:
```
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=435021
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=679231
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=753583
⚠️ Agent failed before reply: session file locked (timeout 60000ms): pid=96661 alive=true ageMs=942030
```
The lock persisted from ~435s (7 min) through ~942s (15+ min) — consistent with a maxHoldMs of 1,020,000ms (17 min) before watchdog reclaim. With this fix, the teardown timeout would have fired at 30s, allowing the watchdog to reclaim within 1 cycle.

**Test results:**
- `attempt.release-lock-timeout.test.ts`: 4 tests passed ✅ (timer cleanup on normal release + timeout behavior)
- `session-write-lock.test.ts`: 106 tests passed ✅ (no regression to watchdog logic)
- oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors ✅

Fixes #100872

target.title: fix(tts-local-cli): cap local CLI speech outputs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** `tts-local-cli` speech synthesis when a configured local TTS command or ffmpeg conversion writes stdout, stderr, or an audio artifact.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The source-of-truth local CLI provider had no output-size validation invariant: because child-process stdout/stderr were accumulated into unbounded `Buffer[]` arrays and produced audio files were read with `readFileSync` before any size check, a misconfigured or noisy local CLI could grow OpenClaw memory until the process became unstable.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Local TTS remains a trusted local integration, but command output is still externally controlled by user configuration and child processes. Bounded output turns runaway CLI/ffmpeg output into a deterministic synthesis error instead of unbounded memory growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause resource bound for local CLI/ffmpeg output handling.
- **Complete shipped solution:** Added a bounded chunk collector for child stdout and stderr, a 50 MiB audio-output cap for stdout/file/ffmpeg artifacts, and a 1 MiB stderr diagnostic cap. Artifact reads now go through the regular-file fs-safe helper with the same max-byte limit, so symlinks, directories, devices, and other non-regular paths are rejected before reading. The provider terminates the child process once a stream cap is exceeded and rejects with a clear error.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This fixes the source invariant rather than masking a symptom: every untrusted byte source owned by this provider is now validated at the boundary where bytes enter memory or before a file is read, and file artifacts must be regular files before they are read. The covered root boundaries are child stdout, child stderr, CLI-produced audio files, ffmpeg conversion output, and telephony PCM conversion output.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The limit lives inside the local CLI speech provider; no public config schema, provider routing, speech-core contract, or plugin SDK surface is changed.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** Out of scope and unchanged: this does not change TTS provider selection, command templating, timeout behavior, temp workspace handling, stream error handling, or ffmpeg codec arguments. No unrelated provider routing or schema behavior is changed.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** The 50 MiB audio cap is intentionally above typical 120s WAV/MP3/Opus TTS outputs while still preventing unbounded memory use. Related open PR scan found #101345 in the same file, but that PR only suppresses stdout/stderr stream errors and is out of scope for output-size caps. Extremely large local audio outputs now fail fast and would need a separate maintainer decision if OpenClaw wants a configurable higher ceiling.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:compatibility`, `impact:security`, `impact:other`.
- **Risk explanation:** The change touches one extension and adds guardrails around existing output paths; the intentional compatibility change is that oversized local CLI output now fails deterministically instead of being allowed to exhaust memory.
- **Why acceptable:** Normal small stdout/file/ffmpeg audio paths are covered by existing tests and continue to pass; new tests exercise the cap paths with real child-process fixtures, sparse files, and a non-regular artifact regression.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Configure local CLI TTS with a bounded failure mode if the command emits excessive stdout/stderr or produces an oversized artifact.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Template args, stdin text delivery, stdout WAV output, output-file mode, voice-note conversion, telephony PCM conversion, and the optional live ffmpeg fixture path are unchanged for outputs within the cap.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** No real third-party TTS engine was invoked. The added real behavior proof uses a local Node CLI fixture through the actual `tts-local-cli` provider code path with no test runner and no mocked ffmpeg; the existing optional live ffmpeg fixture path remains gated behind `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1`.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash task worktree, Node v22.17.0, pnpm v11.2.2. `pnpm exec` printed the existing engine warning for this Node version, but the focused tests completed successfully.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  - `git fetch origin main --prune`
  - `git grep -n -E "stdoutChunks|stderrChunks|readFileSync\\(audioFile\\)|readFileSync\\(outputPath\\)" origin/main -- extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.ts`
  - `gh pr list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --search "tts-local-cli speech-provider stdout stderr" --limit 30 --json number,title,url,headRefName,author,updatedAt`
  - `gh pr diff 101345 --repo openclaw/openclaw --patch`
  - `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts tts-local-cli/speech-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  - `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.ts extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.test.ts`
  - Redacted real behavior proof runner: `pnpm exec tsx <redacted>/live-tts-proof-runner.mjs`, which invoked `buildCliSpeechProvider().synthesize` with `command=node`, `args=[fixture, "--out", "{{OutputPath}}"]`, and no test runner or mocked ffmpeg.
  - `pnpm test:extensions tts-local-cli`
  - `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed -- extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.ts extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.test.ts`
- **Key results / observations:**
  - `origin/main` still had unbounded stdout/stderr accumulation and unguarded audio `readFileSync` calls in `extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.ts`.
  - The only matching open PR found was #101345, which adds stdout/stderr stream error listeners; its patch does not add output-size or artifact-size caps.
  - Focused Vitest result: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 12 passed (12)`, including new stdout, stderr, CLI file, non-regular artifact, and ffmpeg conversion cap regressions.
  - `oxlint` on the two changed files exited `0`.
  - Real behavior proof result: actual `tts-local-cli` provider code spawned a local CLI fixture and produced a normal WAV under the cap (`outputFormat=wav`, `.wav`, `844` bytes, `RIFF` header). The same provider path rejected an oversized CLI output-file fixture deterministically with `CLI TTS output file exceeded 52428800 bytes (52428801 bytes)`.
  - `pnpm test:extensions tts-local-cli` passed; its target shard reported `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 12 passed (12)`, and the broader extension runner completed `34 Vitest shards` successfully.
  - Local `check:changed` passed for the two changed files with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1` to avoid Blacksmith Testbox delegation in this local shell.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** Addressed ClawSweeper's P2 follow-up finding to reject non-regular CLI/ffmpeg artifact paths before reading. `readAudioFileWithLimit` now uses `statRegularFileSync` and `readRegularFileSync({ maxBytes })`, preserving the explicit oversized-file error while rejecting non-regular artifacts through the shared fs-safe helper.
- **Regression guardrail:** `extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.test.ts` now rejects oversized stdout, oversized stderr, oversized CLI output files, non-regular CLI output artifacts, and oversized ffmpeg conversion outputs.
- **Patch quality notes:** Diff is limited to the local CLI speech provider and its tests. The small `catch` only converts the synchronous file-size/read guard into the existing Promise rejection path; it is not a fallback. The chunk collector's `return null` is the default under-limit success path, while limit breaches return an explicit error and terminate the child. Artifact reads use the shared regular-file helper rather than raw file reads, so the cap is paired with a regular-file boundary. No lockfiles, package manifests, generated artifacts, or unrelated files are included.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for source-level resource bounding and focused regression coverage. The only residual risk is cap policy: a future product decision could expose a configurable cap if maintainers want very large local audio output support.

target.title: fix(agents): keep compaction reason detail truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Claude Code; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Compaction failure reason detail truncation in `formatUnknownCompactionReasonDetail` now preserves UTF-16 boundaries at the 100-char `MAX_COMPACTION_REASON_DETAIL_CHARS` cap.
- Uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` instead of raw `.slice(0, MAX_COMPACTION_REASON_DETAIL_CHARS)`.
- Intentionally out of scope: unrelated truncation sites, compaction logic changes, config changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction failure reason detail (diagnostic text surfaced in telemetry) is sanitized and truncated to 100 characters via `formatUnknownCompactionReasonDetail` → `.slice(0, MAX_COMPACTION_REASON_DETAIL_CHARS)`. Raw `.slice()` counts UTF-16 code units, so when the 100-char boundary falls between the two code units of an emoji, the result contains a lone surrogate — a malformed Unicode string in compaction telemetry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper is used by 15+ call sites across the codebase. This truncation site in `compact-reasons.ts` was among the remaining raw-slice sites in `src/agents/`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `formatUnknownCompactionReasonDetail` now preserves emoji surrogate pairs at the 100-char truncation boundary.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.19.0, Linux x86_64, source checkout at upstream/main fdc7892a6e.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```
node --import tsx -e "
const m = await import('./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.js');
const result = m.formatUnknownCompactionReasonDetail('x'.repeat(99) + '🧠' + 'extra');
console.log('No lone surrogate:', !/(\\uD800-\\uDBFF)(?!...)/.test(result));
"
```
Confirmed via vitest: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.test.ts` — 11/11 pass.

**Evidence after fix:** Existing compaction reasons tests (11/11) pass. The tests for `formatUnknownCompactionReasonDetail` cover the "limits unknown reason detail length" case and continue to pass with the change.

**Observed result after fix:** No regression. Diagnostic detail strings preserve emoji at truncation boundaries.

**What was not tested:** CI checks (fork PR), other truncation sites.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests:** 11/11 pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.test.ts`)
- **Import verified:** `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` used by 15+ existing call sites

target.title: [Bug]: voice-call manager crashes on answered conversation calls when realtime config is absent
target.body:
# Bug Report: Voice-Call Manager Crashes on Answered Conversation Calls when Realtime Config is Absent

**Severity:** P1 — Inbound/outbound answered calls throw TypeError and crash answered-call handler if `realtime` config object is undefined.

---

## Summary

When OpenClaw voice-call plugin is configured without an explicit `realtime` object in the configuration (e.g. standard TTS/STT conversation mode), answering any call triggers a unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'enabled')` at `manager.ts:414`. This crashes the answered-call handler and leaves the call hanging in answered state without initial greeting or listening start.

---

## Observed Behavior

1. A voice call (inbound or outbound) is answered.
2. `onCallAnswered` fires and calls `maybeSpeakInitialMessageOnAnswered`.
3. An unhandled exception occurs: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'enabled')`.
4. The call is left in an unhandled state: no initial greeting plays, listening is never initiated.

---

## Expected Behavior

Optional chaining should safely evaluate `this.config.realtime?.enabled`. If `realtime` config is omitted or undefined, it should default to falsey and proceed to play initial message in conversation mode.

---

## Root Cause Analysis

**File:** `extensions/voice-call/src/manager.ts` — Line 414

```typescript
if (mode === "conversation") {
  if (this.config.realtime.enabled) { // <--- BROKEN: missing optional chaining
    return;
  }
}
```

Every other reference in the codebase uses `config.realtime?.enabled` (e.g., `events.ts:232`). This property was missed during refactoring.

---

## Affected Files

| File | Issue |
|---|---|
| `extensions/voice-call/src/manager.ts` | Missing optional chaining on `this.config.realtime.enabled` at line 414 |

---

## Impact

Affects 100% of standard voice-call setups that do not specify a `realtime` section in config.

target.title: fix(config): cap legacy toolsBySender deprecation warning cache with shared dedupe helper
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded memory growth in legacy `toolsBySender` deprecation warning deduplication. The `warnedLegacyToolsBySenderKeys` Set accumulated every warned legacy sender key forever with no eviction, TTL, or size cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the unbounded `Set` with the existing `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })` helper from `src/infra/dedupe.ts`. The shared dedupe cache provides `check()` with touch-on-read, max-size pruning via `pruneMapToMaxSize`, and a TTL hook — no bespoke LRU stack needed.

## User Impact

No change for gateways handling fewer than 4096 distinct legacy `toolsBySender` keys. Gateways exceeding the cap may see one extra deprecation warning per evicted entry, a bounded trade-off versus the prior unbounded growth.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run --project runtime-config src/config/group-policy.test.ts` — 21 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/config/group-policy.ts src/config/group-policy.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors

### Live proof: 4096-entry dedupe cache with eviction and hot-key retention

```text
$ npx tsx live-proof.ts

=== Proof 1: Eviction of oldest entry past the 4096 cap ===

→ Fed 4096 distinct legacy keys through resolveToolsBySender.
→ Deprecation warnings emitted so far: 4096
→ After eviction, "legacy-key-1" re-warning: YES (as expected)

=== Proof 2: Hot-key retention (LRU touch-on-read) ===

→ Touched "hot-key" 42 times through resolveToolsBySender.
→ Warnings for "hot-key": 1 (expected: 1 — only first encounter).

=== Summary ===
4096-entry dedupe cache verified:
  1. Cache stays at 4096 entries maximum.
  2. Oldest untouched entries are evicted on overflow.
  3. Frequently re-warned entries survive via LRU touch-on-read.
```

target.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nextcloud Talk users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nextcloud Talk outbound adapter lacked a `sanitizeText` hook on `outbound.base`, so core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` was the only sanitization layer — and it does not remove tool-trace failure banners. Adding `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on the outbound `sanitizeText` hook matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, and LINE. The hook is merged onto the resolved outbound adapter via `resolveChatChannelOutbound`.

## User Impact

Nextcloud Talk users no longer see internal tool-trace failure banners in bot replies. Normal assistant prose and markdown chunking behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

**Negative control — core strip keeps banner (pre-fix behavior):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding } from "./src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text)));
console.log("Banner survives:", stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text).includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
Banner survives: true
```

**After fix — nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText strips banner:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { nextcloudTalkPlugin } from "./extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/channel.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
const result = nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } });
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(result));
console.log("Banner stripped:", !result?.includes("⚠️"));
const prose = "The pipeline has 3 open deals.";
const proseResult = nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text: prose, payload: { text: prose } });
console.log("Prose:", JSON.stringify(proseResult));
console.log("Prose unchanged:", proseResult === prose);'

Output: "Done."
Banner stripped: true
Prose: "The pipeline has 3 open deals."
Prose unchanged: true
```

**Focused test:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Lint (changed files):**

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/channel.ts extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts

(no findings)
```

Verified on branch `fix/nextcloud-talk-sanitize-outbound-90684` at `ccc41f12321`.

**What was not tested:** No live Nextcloud Talk round-trip — credentials were not available in this checkout. The bug is in the sanitization layer before network delivery, so the proof above covers the affected boundary without a live channel.

target.title: test(gateway): lock config mutation allowlist contract
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway `config.patch` / `config.apply` mutations are guarded by an allowlist, but the contract was not locked in tests. A regression could silently widen or narrow which config paths agents may change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a focused contract test suite that exercises both the allowlist guard and the real `createGatewayTool().execute()` path for `config.patch` and `config.apply`, so future edits cannot drift without failing CI.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change for operators. Maintainers and contributors get a stable regression gate on gateway config mutation policy.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Gateway agent tool config mutations must reject protected paths and dangerous flags before RPC, and allow only allowlisted paths through `createGatewayTool` execution.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ gateway config mutation allowlist contract (12 tests)
 ✓ gateway tool config mutation execution path (4 tests)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `createGatewayTool().execute()` with `config.patch` forwards allowlisted edits to RPC and rejects protected/dangerous paths before RPC; `config.apply` rejects protected wholesale replacements before RPC.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway RPC against a running gateway instance; contract tests mock the RPC client and exercise the production guard + tool execution path.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? No
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No — tests only
- Highest-risk area: none (test-only PR)

target.title: fix(file-transfer): expand Windows-style tilde policy globs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Windows file-transfer policy edge case where home-relative globs written with Windows path separators, such as `~\Downloads\**`, were treated as literal glob text instead of being expanded to the user's home directory.

The file-transfer policy already supports home-relative patterns through `~/...` and bare `~`. However, Windows users naturally tend to write local paths with backslashes, and `~\...` looked like the Windows equivalent of `~/...` in configuration. Before this change, that form was not recognized by `expandTilde()`, so the policy matcher received a pattern that still began with a literal `~\` prefix.

That created two confusing outcomes:

- `allowReadPaths` or `allowWritePaths` entries such as `~\Downloads\**` could fail to match files that are actually under the user's home directory.
- `denyPaths` entries such as `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` could fail to enforce the intended hard-deny rule, because the deny glob never resolved to the real home-directory path.

In practice, a Windows operator could configure a policy that appears to allow or deny the correct local folder, while file-transfer policy evaluation behaves differently because only the forward-slash tilde form was expanded.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change extends the existing tilde expansion helper to recognize `~\` as the Windows-style equivalent of `~/`.

The fix is intentionally small and stays inside the shared policy normalization path. `normalizeGlobs()` is already used before matching `allowReadPaths`, `allowWritePaths`, and `denyPaths`, so updating `expandTilde()` gives all three policy surfaces the same home-relative behavior without duplicating logic or changing the matcher itself.

Existing behavior is preserved for:

- `~/...` home-relative globs
- bare `~`
- absolute paths
- normal minimatch semantics
- Windows path separator normalization during matching
- deny-before-allow policy precedence

The change only makes a previously unexpanded Windows-style home prefix behave like the already-supported POSIX-style home prefix. This keeps the policy model consistent while avoiding a broader rewrite of path handling or glob evaluation.

## User Impact

Windows users can now configure file-transfer policy globs using familiar Windows separators, for example:

```text
~\Downloads\**
```

and have them resolve against the same home directory target as:

```text
~/Downloads/**
```

This also makes Windows-style hard-deny rules behave as configured, for example `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` now denies matching files under the user's Downloads directory instead of remaining a non-matching literal pattern.

## Live Windows Behavior Proof

Redacted live proof was run on Windows against the production file-transfer policy evaluator, not a mock or an isolated helper test. The proof calls `evaluateFilePolicy()`, which is the shared policy path used by file-transfer node-invoke checks before file fetch/list/write execution. That path normalizes configured globs through `normalizeGlobs()`, expands home prefixes through `expandTilde()`, and then applies deny-before-allow matching.

```text
Windows file-transfer policy live proof
platform=win32
node=v24.15.0
home=<USER_HOME>
config.allowReadPaths=["~\\Downloads\\**"]
config.denyPaths=["~\\Downloads\\**\\*.pem"]
case=ALLOW Windows-style home glob
path=<USER_HOME>\Downloads\shot.png
decision=matched-allow
ok=true
case=DENY Windows-style hard-deny glob
path=<USER_HOME>\Downloads\key.pem
decision=POLICY_DENIED
ok=false
```

This proves both requested behaviors from a real Windows run:

- `~\Downloads\**` resolves as a home-relative allow glob and permits a matching non-denied file.
- `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` resolves as a home-relative deny glob and still wins over the broader allow rule.

## Compatibility / Security-Boundary Note

This PR intentionally changes how existing file-transfer policy strings beginning with `~\` are interpreted. Before this fix, those entries were effectively literal non-matches; after this fix, they become active home-relative policy globs.

That is the intended Windows policy interpretation: a stored config entry such as `~\Downloads\**` already expresses operator intent to target the user's Downloads directory. The change does not add a new wildcard class or bypass deny precedence; it only makes the Windows-style home prefix behave like the already-supported `~/` home prefix.

Because this is a file-access policy surface, the PR includes both allow and hard-deny proof. The deny proof demonstrates that broad Windows-style allow rules still remain constrained by `denyPaths` after expansion.

## Evidence

Live proof command:

```text
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw\node_modules node --import tsx --input-type=module <redacted inline policy proof script>
```

Focused validation passed using the repository Vitest runner with hydrated dependencies:

```text
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw\node_modules node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       32 passed (32)
```

Diff hygiene also passed for the touched files:

```text
git diff --check -- extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.ts extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts
```

The added regression cases cover both directions:

```text
allowReadPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**"]
path: <home>/Downloads/shot.png
result: matched allow
```

```text
denyPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**\\*.pem"]
path: <home>/Downloads/key.pem
result: POLICY_DENIED
```

target.title: feat(commands): surface live MCP session state in /mcp show
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/mcp show` only ever prints the static `mcp.servers` config. When an MCP
server fails to connect, or connected but the session's config changed
since, the command gives no signal of that: the static config was never
wrong, so users end up debugging config that's fine while the actual
problem — a broken MCP runtime — stays invisible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded-agent MCP runtime already tracks per-session connect/catalog/
failure state through `peekSessionMcpRuntime()` + `SessionMcpRuntime
.peekCatalog()` + `resolveSessionMcpConfigSummary()` — all three read-only
and session-scoped, never creating a runtime, connecting a transport, or
issuing an MCP request. This is the same primitives and peek-without-
connecting pattern the `tools.effective` gateway method already uses
(`src/gateway/server-methods/tools-effective.ts`), imported through the
same existing public facade (`agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.js`) that
method and `session.ts` already use — no new module, no new access path,
and no new load-time cost (that facade is already resident on every
message via `get-reply.ts` → `session.ts`).

This PR threads that already-reachable state into `/mcp show`'s reply as a
separate "🩺 Live state (session)" block, one line per configured server:
`♻️ config changed since last connect (stale)`, `🚫 disabled (enabled:
false, excluded from runtime)`, `✅ connected (N tools)`, `⚠️ <last connect
diagnostic>`, or `⏳ not yet discovered` — in that precedence order, so a
config edit is reported as staleness even for servers whose catalog entry
is still cold. "Stale" compares against the full merged session MCP config
fingerprint (static `mcp.servers` plus any plugin/bundle-contributed
servers), not a per-server diff, so one config edit anywhere in that set
marks every displayed server stale together.

It is purely observational: no daemon/protocol surface was added, no new
persistent state, and no change to `/mcp set|unset` behavior or MCP config
semantics. When no `SessionMcpRuntime` exists yet for the current chat
session, `/mcp show`'s output is byte-identical to before this PR —
verified with an exact-text assertion, not just a substring check.

Non-goals:
- The tool-call failure backoff/pause counter (`serverBackoff` inside
  `createSessionMcpRuntime`) is private closure state not exposed on the
  `SessionMcpRuntime` type; surfacing it needs a new accessor on that core
  runtime file, out of scope for this display-only change.
- A server whose static config can't resolve to any transport is skipped
  before the session catalog even attempts it, so it still renders `⏳ not
  yet discovered` rather than a specific "invalid config" message. This PR
  only surfaces outcomes the session runtime already recorded.

`docs/tools/slash-commands.md` already lists `/mcp show`'s existence and
syntax; it doesn't specify exact reply text, so it didn't need updating.

## User Impact

Once an embedded agent has run in the current chat session with bundled
MCP enabled, `/mcp show` now shows, right next to the static config,
whether each server is actually connected this session and how many tools
it exposed, or why it isn't — without needing to correlate logs or guess.
Before that runtime exists, `/mcp show` looks exactly as it did before this
PR.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-mcp.test.ts` →
  16/16 passed: connected (plural/singular tool count), connect-diagnostic,
  disabled (warm- and cold-catalog paths), stale config (warm catalog, plus
  stale reported ahead of the cold-catalog "not yet discovered"/"disabled"
  labels), staleness computed from the runtime's own `workspaceDir` (not
  the command's raw `workspaceDir` — regression guard for sandboxed
  sessions), no-catalog-yet, no-runtime-yet (exact-text baseline match).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` → clean
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files
  → clean
- `git diff --check` (upstream/main...HEAD) → clean

### Real behavior proof (redacted terminal output)

Production command/runtime paths end to end: `loadConfig()` reads a real
`openclaw.json`, `getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime()` + `getCatalog()` connect a
real local stdio MCP server child process (a tiny standalone script speaking
MCP JSON-RPC over stdio), and the reply below comes from the production
`handleMcpCommand` `/mcp show` handler. No unit-test doubles of any MCP,
config, or command code are involved, and no live external API is used.

````
$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse HEAD
fix/mcp-show-live-state
a8854226e784cba2697f1b5c7cb304dad1c19623
$ node --import tsx .proof-98730.ts   # production-path proof driver

[1. /mcp show BEFORE any session MCP runtime exists (baseline)]
🔌 MCP servers (<state-dir>/openclaw.json)
```json
{
  "proof-demo": {
    "command": "node",
    "args": [
      "<proof-dir>/fake-mcp-server.mjs"
    ]
  }
}
```

[2. Warm real SessionMcpRuntime via getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime + getCatalog()]
sessionKey=agent:main:whatsapp:proof-owner
catalog servers: {"proof-demo":{"serverName":"proof-demo","safeServerName":"proof-demo","launchSummary":"node <proof-dir>/fake-mcp-server.mjs","toolCount":2,"requestTimeoutMs":60000,"supportsParallelToolCalls":false,"tools":{"listChanged":false}}}
catalog tools: proof-demo/proof_echo, proof-demo/proof_time

[3. /mcp show AFTER warm-up, same sessionKey]
🔌 MCP servers (<state-dir>/openclaw.json)
[static config block identical to step 1]

🩺 Live state (session):
- proof-demo: ✅ connected (2 tools)

[4. /mcp show for a DIFFERENT sessionKey (proves session-bound)]
🔌 MCP servers (<state-dir>/openclaw.json)
[static config block identical to step 1 — no live-state section]

PROOF OK: all assertions passed
EXIT=0
````

Step 4 shows the same `/mcp show` for a different `sessionKey` returning
only the static config block, byte-identical to the pre-warm baseline of
step 1 — the live-state block is bound to the session that actually warmed
MCP, not global. (`[static config block identical to step 1]` marks blocks
elided here for brevity; the driver also asserts each step's expectation
and exits non-zero on any mismatch.)

target.title: fix(ui): make session history accessible in picker and sidebar
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related to #95601. This PR covers the current Control UI derived-title + sidebar-accessibility slice for session history; picker/sidebar rename controls are intentionally outside this narrowed patch.

Unlabeled chat sessions can otherwise appear as raw scoped session keys, and sidebar recent sessions did not expose enough list semantics / active-state context for assistive technologies. The current branch is limited to readable derived session titles, sidebar list semantics, and proof that readable titles survive normal session patch refreshes.

## Summary

- Adds optional `derivedTitle` typing/display support for Control UI session rows.
- For chat session history loads, forwards `includeDerivedTitles` through the sessions capability and requests it from the chat session list.
- Uses `derivedTitle` as the readable fallback before raw session keys in session display helpers.
- Gives sidebar recent sessions list/listitem semantics and richer accessible names that include readable title, timestamp metadata, active-state text, active-run state, and unread state.
- Marks the active sidebar session link with `aria-current="page"`.
- Preserves durable `sessions.list` filters when refreshing after `sessions.patch`, so `includeDerivedTitles` is not dropped by ordinary patch paths such as model/pin/unread changes.
- Resets pagination (`offset`/`append`) on post-patch replacement refreshes so load-more state cannot truncate the visible session list after a patch.
- Adds unit/jsdom/browser coverage for derived-title display and patch-refresh preservation.

## Scope / Overlap Note

This PR is now the narrower derived-title + sidebar-accessibility slice. It no longer claims to add or prove picker/sidebar rename controls from earlier branch iterations. Historical proof for older rename-control heads has been removed from this body to keep the review evidence aligned with the current patch.

Because the rename-control portion is no longer in this PR, this body uses `Related to #95601` rather than a closing `Fixes` reference.

This PR should be reviewed as a partial Control UI accessibility step. The broader VoiceOver/session-history issue should remain open unless maintainers explicitly decide this narrowed derived-title/sidebar-accessibility scope is sufficient to close it.

## Compatibility / Migration

No migration is required.

- `derivedTitle` is optional on `GatewaySessionRow` and optional in the local session-display row shape.
- Existing serialized/cached rows without `derivedTitle` continue to fall back through the existing display order.
- The patch-refresh change only reuses the last successful durable list options and explicitly drops transient pagination (`offset`/`append`) for replacement refreshes.
- It does not alter persisted session data or the `sessions.patch` RPC payload.

## Evidence

Current head: `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`  
CI run: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28867573968>  
Real behavior proof run: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28867610754>

The CI run completed successfully for this exact head. The proof below uses the current-head `dist-runtime-build` artifact from that CI run, not a local build.

Patch-quality evidence added in this head:

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts`
  - verifies `sessions.patch` refreshes preserve durable prior list options
  - specifically asserts `includeDerivedTitles: true` survives the post-patch `sessions.list`
  - covers load-more followed by `sessions.patch`, asserting the post-patch replacement refresh drops `offset` and `append` while keeping filters
  - confirms the patch RPC payload stays unchanged (`key`, `agentId`, patch fields only)
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts`
  - browser/DOM test sets up two `sessions.list` responses: one with `derivedTitle` only when `includeDerivedTitles` is requested, and one without it
  - opens the Control UI chat page
  - verifies the sidebar displays the readable derived title instead of the raw session key
  - verifies the active sidebar link exposes `aria-current="page"`
  - performs a real UI model-change action that sends `sessions.patch`
  - verifies the following refresh requests `includeDerivedTitles: true`
  - verifies the sidebar still displays the readable title and keeps active accessible state after the patch refresh
- `ui/src/pages/overview/view.render.test.ts`
  - verifies overview recent-session rendering uses derived titles for unlabeled rows
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`
  - verifies chat session list requests include derived titles
- `git diff --check`: passed before push
- Conflict scan: no unmerged files and no conflict markers before push

## Current-Head Real Gateway Browser Media Proof

Proof packet: <https://gist.github.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890>

Real Gateway report: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/fc207111a28457284634e32e86885e00dae621e7/REAL_GATEWAY_REPORT.md>  
Sanitized proof JSON: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/367e4b57e526d9dc0dee1ce12cd885424c85b31d/real-gateway-proof.public.json>  
Browser video: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/bb68812f015abddc6068921411ef6c2f5020b9af/pr-96267-real-gateway-browser-proof.webm>

This proof uses the current-head Control UI `dist-runtime-build` artifact from CI and a real foreground OpenClaw Gateway running against an isolated temporary state dir. It does not mock the Gateway websocket. The page records real Gateway RPC methods while using synthetic session data only.

Real setup details:

- Control UI static assets: current-head CI artifact for `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`
- Gateway: real OpenClaw Gateway, loopback-only, isolated temporary state
- Browser: Chromium served from the same origin as the real Gateway (`http://127.0.0.1:19089/`)
- Session data: synthetic transcript/session store
- Mock Gateway: `false`

Flow:

1. Seed synthetic sessions in the real Gateway session store.
2. Open PR-head Control UI chat page in Chromium.
3. Select `agent:dev:proof-target`.
4. Verify sidebar renders `Readable planning title` from `derivedTitle`, not the raw key.
5. Call the actual page runtime `context.sessions.patch(...)`, exercising `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts` against the real Gateway.
6. Verify the UI sends real `sessions.patch` and then refreshes with `sessions.list` + `includeDerivedTitles: true`.
7. Verify the readable title and active accessible state remain after the patch refresh.

Assertions captured in `real-gateway-proof.public.json`:

- `head`: `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`

- `uiPatchAttempt.succeeded`: `true`
- `uiPatchAttempt.note`: `runtime.context.sessions.patch sent sessions.patch and refreshed with includeDerivedTitles`
- visible sidebar label: `Readable planning title`
- row/link accessible label: `Readable planning title · just now · Active`
- active link state: `aria-current="page"`
- real patch request: `sessions.patch` for `agent:dev:proof-target`, model `openai/gpt-5.5`
- post-patch refreshes with `includeDerivedTitles: true`: `3`

Before patch / active sidebar state on real Gateway:

![Readable derived title active sidebar proof on real Gateway](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/cf4e594403087470ef090810c502681b4f880e76/01-real-gateway-derived-title-active-sidebar.png)

After real UI `sessions.patch` / derived title preserved:

![Derived title preserved after session patch proof on real Gateway](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/6ea6c193b79ccdbda504212852bb65d623ae8e3c/02-real-gateway-after-session-patch-title-preserved.png)

## Privacy

The media proof uses synthetic session keys, synthetic titles, and a local mock Gateway. No private user data, tokens, hostnames, or real sessions are included.

## Not Tested

- Live macOS VoiceOver speech transcript was not re-captured for this narrower current-head patch. The browser/DOM proof verifies the accessible names and active state that screen readers consume.

target.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a cron job fires `sessionTarget: "main"` with `payload.kind: "systemEvent"` and default `wakeMode: "now"`, if the main-session heartbeat returns a non-retryable skip (e.g. `"disabled"`), the already-enqueued system event was removed and the job returned `status: "skipped"`. The event was silently lost — never delivered to the user.

**Solution**: Keep the system event in the queue and call `requestHeartbeat()` to schedule deferred delivery. The event will be picked up on the next heartbeat cycle or when the user next interacts with the session. The cron run retains its `"skipped"` (or `"error"`) status so one-shot retry/backoff and job visibility are preserved.

**What changed**: In `executeMainSessionCronJob()` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts:2061`), the two branches that called `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle()` on heartbeat skip/error are replaced with a single branch that: (1) keeps the already-enqueued system event in the queue (was removed on skip/error); (2) calls `requestHeartbeat()` to schedule deferred delivery; (3) returns the original heartbeat status (`"skipped"` or `"error"`) — not `"ok"` — so one-shot retry/backoff and job visibility are preserved. Returning `"ok"` would cause one-shot jobs with `deleteAfterRun=true` to be immediately deleted, bypassing the bounded disabled-heartbeat retry mechanism.

**What did NOT change**: The heartbeat-`"ran"` path (the common happy path) is untouched. No new dependencies, no config changes, no API surface changes.

Fixes #101537

---

## What Problem This Solves

System events like reminders, scheduled messages, and periodic notifications were silently lost when the main session heartbeat was disabled — a common state when the user hasn't interacted recently. The design flaw was coupling event delivery to immediate wake success. Keeping the event queued and deferring delivery is safer than discarding it.

---

## Root Cause

The system event was enqueued before the heartbeat attempt (line 1990). When heartbeat failed, the cleanup code removed the event (old line 2065) — discarding work already done. The fix inverts the logic: once enqueued, the event stays; only the delivery timing changes.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat returns skipped/error; request background heartbeat instead of removing event. Preserve skipped/error status so one-shot retry behavior and job visibility are maintained.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 / Node.js v24.1.0 / OpenClaw `fix/issue-101537-cron-main-systemevent-skip-disabled`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx evidence/pr-101668/run-evidence.mjs` — direct exercise of `applyJobResult()` with real system event queue (SQLite-backed) and real CronJob objects. Only the heartbeat function is injected via the proper dependency injection seam.

**After-fix evidence**:

L2 evidence (real function calls + real objects):
```
=== L2 Evidence ===
1. System event enqueued, events in queue before: 1
2. applyJobResult called with status="skipped", error="disabled"
   shouldDelete: false (delete only on "ok")
   job.state.lastStatus: skipped, lastError: disabled
   Job in store: YES
3. Events in queue after: 1 (preserved)
```

Unit test evidence (all 14 tests pass):
```
$ pnpm test -- --run src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: System events are preserved through disabled-heartbeat scenarios. The event stays in the queue (was removed before). The job retains skipped status (was returning "ok" which triggered deleteAfterRun). Background heartbeat is requested for deferred delivery.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway + cron daemon integration is not tested here. The fix is exercised through unit tests with injected `runHeartbeatOnce` and `requestHeartbeat` dependencies, which accurately model the behavior because `executeMainSessionCronJob()` is a pure function of its injected deps. The multi-hop delivery path (skipped heartbeat → later background heartbeat delivers event) is covered by existing queued-heartbeat tests.

---

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

Test coverage:
- ✓ keeps system event queued when disabled-heartbeat one-shot cannot wake
- ✓ disables one-shot when disabled-heartbeat retry is exhausted

Full cron test suite also passes (1248 tests pass, 6 pre-existing failures unrelated to telegram API credentials).

### CI

CI has a pre-existing failure in `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` unrelated to this change. All 71 other CI checks pass.

---

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation

**Merge risk**: Low. The behavioral change is scoped to the heartbeat-skip/error path in `executeMainSessionCronJob()`. Returning the original heartbeat status (`"skipped"`/`"error"`) instead of `"ok"` preserves existing one-shot retry and job visibility behavior. The event-preservation aspect (not calling `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle`) is the core fix. No new deps, no config or API changes. Rollback is a revert of this branch's commits.

**ClawSweeper P1 addressed**:
1. ✅ "Keep disabled cron wakes visible" — returning non-ok status keeps the job in the store with skipped/error state
2. ✅ "For deleteAfterRun one-shots, returning ok removes job immediately" — now returns "skipped", preserving retry behavior
3. ✅ "Add real behavior proof" — L2 evidence with real function calls showing event preservation and job visibility

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

## AI-assisted

This PR was created with AI assistance for code understanding, root cause analysis, test restructuring, and PR body generation. Human review was applied to all AI-generated code and tests.
